Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: ZamPortal (zamportal.gov.zm / eservices.gov.zm) uses ZamPass authentication service, where users log in with their NRC or Passport ID number and password. The portal offers access to ~300 of ~1,500 government services. ZamPass is the governmental authentication service for portal access. The NRC number is the primary identifier for government portal authentication.
revision_notes: Confirmed live: ZamPass (pass.gsb.gov.zm) is operational as Zambia's National Authentication and Access Control Service, and ZamPortal's own FAQ pages describe sign-in via ZamPass using NRC number, password, hardware key or passkey. The originally cited ZamPass PDF guide returned a 403 error on fetch but its content is corroborated by the live portal pages. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Zambia operates a centralised government authentication gateway, ZamPass (pass.gsb.gov.zm), which enables citizens and residents to sign in using their nine-digit NRC number or a passport number, alongside password, hardware key or passkey options. ZamPass underpins authentication for the ZamPortal e-services platform (eservices.gov.zm/zamportal.gov.zm), which provides access to several hundred government services from a single website.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2021 provides data subjects with rights to access their personal data held by data controllers. However, there is no documented digital self-service portal or mechanism for individuals to view their own ID-system data online. ZamPortal provides access to government services but individual data viewing within the INRIS system is not publicly documented. Enforcement of DPA data access rights remains weak per Strathmore/CIPIT 2025 assessment.
revision_notes: The Data Protection Act PDF (szi.gov.zm) returned an HTTP 403 error on fetch and could not be directly verified, but its existence and provisions are independently corroborated by other sources. The CIPIT/Strathmore October 2025 report on digital ID and government digital services in Zambia was fetched and confirms enforcement of data subject rights remains weak, with no self-service portal for individuals to view their ID-system data documented. Score of 1 (No) upheld.
revised_comments: Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 grants data subjects a statutory right to access personal data held by data controllers, but no dedicated self-service portal, mobile app or other mechanism allowing individuals to view their identity-system data or access logs online is publicly documented. A 2025 CIPIT/Strathmore assessment of government digital services and digital ID in Zambia finds that enforcement of data subject rights, including access, remains weak in practice.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Zambia's general judicial system provides oversight through courts but there are no ID-specific judicial mechanisms identified. The Data Protection Act 2021 provides a complaints/investigation mechanism via the Data Protection Commissioner rather than courts. The e-Government Act 2021 includes penalties for offences but no dedicated ID court oversight mechanism has been documented.
revision_notes: The Electronic Government Act 2021 was fetched directly and confirms establishment of an e-government division, data protection provisions (Section 20) and information security rules, but no ID-specific judicial review or tribunal mechanism. General constitutional court oversight applies to all administrative decisions, including those of the ID authority, consistent with the original score. The Data Protection Act PDF returned a 403 error and could not be directly re-verified, but its general complaints mechanism via the Data Protection Commissioner is well corroborated elsewhere. Score of 2 (Yes, but not specific to ID) upheld.
revised_comments: Decisions of Zambia's identity and civil registration authorities are subject to the general oversight of the ordinary courts under constitutional and administrative law, as with all public bodies. Neither the National Registration Act nor the Electronic Government Act 2021 establishes an ID-specific judicial review mechanism or tribunal; complaints relating to data handling are instead directed in the first instance to the Data Protection Commissioner under the Data Protection Act 2021.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Zambia enacted the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 (assented 23 March 2021). It establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner, regulates collection/processing/storage of personal and biometric data, provides data subject rights, and requires registration of data controllers. Mr Likando Lyuwa was appointed as the first Data Protection Commissioner in 2023.
revision_notes: The Data Protection Act PDF (szi.gov.zm) returned a 403 error on direct fetch, but the Paradigm Initiative Londa 2023 country report (fetched, published April 2024) independently confirms the Data Protection Act 2021 is in force and that the Data Protection Office/Commissioner has been established. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 provides the national legal framework for personal data protection, including biometric data collected for identity purposes. It establishes data subject rights, obligations on data controllers, and a registration requirement, and applies to personal data linked to the digital identity system.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Commission was established under the Data Protection Act 2021. Mr Likando Lyuwa was appointed as the first Data Protection Commissioner in June 2023. The Commission expressed concern over hacking incidents in financial institutions (July 2023). Training of staff in 145+ offices on the Data Protection Act is ongoing. The Commissioner enforces the DPA, investigates complaints, and issues guidelines.
revision_notes: Both sources were fetched and confirm the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act 2021, with a Commissioner appointed in 2023. The UNDP blog (September 2024) confirms the Commission remains actively engaged in Zambia's ongoing digital ID and DPI governance work. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Zambia's Data Protection Commission, established under the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, regulates the collection, processing and sharing of personal data, including biometric data collected by the national identity system. A Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in 2023, and UNDP reporting from September 2024 confirms the Commission remains actively engaged as Zambia advances the governance framework around its digital ID and broader digital public infrastructure.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The National Registration Card is established as legal proof of identity under the National Registration Act. The Electronic Government Act 2021 (Section 21) explicitly provides that public bodies shall offer 'electronic proof of identity issued under the National Registration Act' in administrative procedures. The NRC is accepted for banking (KYC), SIM registration, and government service access.
revision_notes: Both sources fetched directly. The Electronic Government Act 2021's table of contents confirms Section 21 ('Identity and authenticity') and Section 24 ('Citizen card') exist, consistent with the cited claim regarding electronic proof of identity issued under the National Registration Act. mohais.gov.zm confirms the NRC is the standard government-issued proof-of-identity document required for citizens aged 16+. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: The National Registration Card, issued under the National Registration Act (Cap 126), is Zambia's legally recognised proof of identity, required for accessing banking, SIM registration and government services. The Electronic Government Act No. 41 of 2021 additionally addresses identity and authenticity (Section 21) and citizen cards (Section 24), requiring public bodies to accept electronic proof of identity issued under the National Registration Act in administrative procedures.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under the National Registration Act (Cap 126), the NRC applies to all persons who have attained age 16. The Ministry of Home Affairs website and April 2025 nationwide NRC campaign confirm eligibility at 16 years and above. The new digital ID system also targets adults 16+. Child registration for early legal identity is planned as a future improvement under INRIS.
revision_notes: All three sources were fetched directly. The National Registration Act, Section 3, confirms the Act applies to persons who 'attain...the age of sixteen years'. mohais.gov.zm and an April 2025 Biometric Update article both confirm 16 as the minimum eligibility age for NRC/digital ID registration. Under the variable's scale (1 = >17; 2 = 10-17; 3 = 6-10; 4 = 1-5; 5 = <1), an eligibility age of 16 falls within the '10-17' band, i.e. code 2, not code 1 (>17) as originally recorded — the original Comments text itself states age 16 but the Value Code was inconsistent with it. Value Code corrected to 2.
revised_comments: Individuals become eligible to register for Zambia's National Registration Card, the country's foundational identity credential, on attaining 16 years of age, as set out in the National Registration Act (Cap 126) and confirmed in current Ministry of Home Affairs guidance and the 2025 nationwide enrolment campaign. There is no separate, earlier-age enrolment pathway; registration for the NRC/digital ID begins at age 16.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The National Registration Act (Cap 126, Section 3 and 6) requires all persons aged 16+ within specified areas to register. Registration is compulsory under Zambian law - unregistered persons entering a specified area must register within 14 days. Birth registration is also compulsory under the Birth and Death Registration Act. The NRC is mandatory for all eligible citizens.
revision_notes: The National Registration Act, Section 3 (fetched directly), confirms mandatory application to all persons aged 16+ within a specified area, subject only to narrow exemptions (armed forces, accredited diplomats, short-term visitors). mohais.gov.zm confirms compulsory registration requirements, and an April 2025 nationwide mobile enrolment campaign (Biometric Update) demonstrates active, ongoing enforcement. Score of 3 (Mandatory for all) upheld.
revised_comments: Registration for Zambia's National Registration Card is mandatory for all persons aged 16 and above within a specified area under the National Registration Act (Cap 126), with only narrow exemptions for armed forces personnel, accredited diplomats and short-term visitors. The requirement is actively enforced through nationwide mobile enrolment campaigns, such as the one launched in April 2025 targeting 3.5 million citizens.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration with national ID (NRC or passport) has been mandatory in Zambia since 2013 under the ICT Act No. 15 of 2009 and SI No. 65 of 2011. ZICTA enforced mandatory registration with a December 2013 deadline; non-compliant SIMs were deactivated by February 2014. MTN Zambia requires Green NRC or passport for SIM registration. A SIM registration campaign relaunch was announced in 2025. Zambia requires national ID for all SIM cards.
revision_notes: The original citation dated to the 2013 introduction of the policy; this has been refreshed with current evidence. MTN Zambia's live SIM registration page (fetched, updated December 2024) confirms Green NRC or a valid passport is required for registration. ZICTA maintains an active SIM registration consumer-protection page, and an August 2025 Zambia Monitor report confirms ZICTA continues to actively enforce registration rules, blocking unregistered or fraud-linked SIM cards and capping registrations at 10 per person. Score of 3 (Mandatory) upheld; year updated to reflect current enforcement rather than the original 2013 policy date.
revised_comments: SIM card registration using a national identity document (Green NRC or a valid passport) is mandatory for mobile service activation in Zambia, a requirement in force since 2013 under the ICT Act and its subsidiary regulations. Mobile network operators such as MTN require presentation of an NRC or passport for registration, and the regulator ZICTA continues to actively enforce compliance, including blocking unregistered or fraudulently registered SIM cards and capping the number of SIMs an individual may register.
